questions.title: Switch Expression Types
questions.description: In a classic Java 8 style switch statement, which of the following types can NOT be used directly as the switch expression?

questions.title: Role of break in a switch
questions.description: What happens when a break statement executes inside a switch case?
questions.Option1: Control jumps to the next case below
questions.Option2: Control exits the switch statement and continues after it
questions.Option4: The switch starts matching again from the first case

questions.title: Role of continue in a loop
questions.description: In a Java loop, what does the continue statement do?
questions.Option2: It skips the remaining statements of the current iteration and proceeds with the next iteration
questions.Option4: It resets the loop variable and restarts the loop from the first iteration

questions.title: Condition Type of if
questions.description: In Java, the condition written inside an if statement must be of which type?
questions.Option1: int, where 0 means false and any other value means true
questions.Option3: any numeric type, where nonzero means true
questions.Option4: String, where the text true means true

questions.title: Placement of the default Label
questions.description: In a classic Java switch block, where may the default label appear?
questions.Option1: Only as the very last label of the switch block
questions.Option2: Only as the very first label of the switch block
questions.Option3: Anywhere among the cases, because case matching depends on labels, not on position
questions.Option4: Only immediately after the first case label

questions.title: else-if Ladder Execution Rule
questions.description: In an else-if ladder, several conditions happen to be true at the same time. How many branches execute?
questions.Option1: All the true branches execute from top to bottom
questions.Option2: Only the first true branch executes and the rest of the ladder is skipped
questions.Option3: Only the last true branch executes
questions.Option4: The ladder re-evaluates every condition from bottom to top

questions.title: Ternary to if-else Conversion
questions.description: The conditional operator can replace a simple if-else assignment. Which if-else block is equivalent to: int max = (a > b) ? a : b;
questions.Option1: int max; if (a > b) { max = a; } else { max = b; }
questions.Option2: int max; if (a > b) { max = b; } else { max = a; }
questions.Option3: int max = a; if (a > b) { max = b; }
questions.Option4: int max; if (a >= b) { max = b; } else { max = a; }

questions.title: Switch With No Matching Case
questions.description: A switch statement has no default label and none of its case labels matches the switched value. What happens?
questions.Option2: The whole switch is skipped and execution continues with the statement after it
questions.Option3: The first case executes as a fallback

questions.title: Nested if Evaluation Order
questions.description: An if statement is nested inside the body of another if statement. When is the inner if condition evaluated?
questions.Option1: Always, regardless of the outer condition
questions.Option2: Only when the outer condition is true
questions.Option3: Only when the outer condition is false
questions.Option4: Only if the inner condition was true during a previous run

questions.title: break versus continue
questions.description: Which statement best distinguishes break from continue in Java?
questions.Option1: break skips to the next iteration while continue exits the loop entirely
questions.Option2: break exits the enclosing loop or switch entirely, while continue only skips the remaining statements of the current iteration
questions.Option3: Both statements terminate the program immediately
questions.Option4: continue works only inside switch statements, while break works only inside loops
